cards.back: The "fair share" average. Add all the values, then divide by how many there are. Example: 2, 4, 6 has mean 12 ÷ 3 = 4.
cards.say: Mean. The "fair share" average. Add all the values, then divide by how many there are. Example: two, four, six has mean twelve divided by three equals four.

cards.back: The value that appears most often. Example: in 3, 5, 5, 8, 9 the mode is 5.
cards.say: Mode. The value that appears most often. Example: in three, five, five, eight, nine the mode is five.

cards.back: The middle value when the numbers are in order. Example: in 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 the median is 7.
cards.say: Median. The middle value when the numbers are in order. Example: in three, five, seven, nine, eleven the median is seven.

cards.back: The biggest value minus the smallest value. It shows how spread out the data is.
cards.say: Range. The biggest value minus the smallest value. It shows how spread out the data is.

cards.back: 6. The total is 30 and 30 ÷ 5 = 6.
cards.say: Find the mean of three, five, five, eight, nine. Six. The total is thirty and thirty divided by five equals six.

cards.back: 5. It is the middle value of the five numbers.
cards.say: Find the median of three, five, five, eight, nine. Five. It is the middle value of the five numbers.
Find the range of three, five, five, eight, nine. Six. Nine minus three equals six.

cards.back: 6. With two middle numbers (5 and 7), find the number halfway between them.
cards.say: Find the median of three, five, seven, nine. Six. With two middle numbers, five and seven, find the number halfway between them.

cards.back: 4. The two middle numbers are both 4.
cards.say: Find the median of two, four, four, ten. Four. The two middle numbers are both four.

cards.back: 5. The total is 20 and 20 ÷ 4 = 5.
cards.say: Find the mean of two, four, four, ten. Five. The total is twenty and twenty divided by four equals five.

cards.back: 6. It appears 3 times, more than any other number.
cards.say: Find the mode of six, two, six, nine, two, six. Six. It appears three times, more than any other number.

cards.front: Can a set of data have no mode?
cards.back: Yes, if every value appears only once. It can also have two modes.
cards.say: Can a set of data have no mode? Yes, if every value appears only once. It can also have two modes.

cards.front: The mean of 5 numbers is 8. What is their total?
cards.back: 40. Mean × how many = total, so 8 × 5 = 40.
cards.say: The mean of five numbers is eight. What is their total? Forty. Mean times how many equals total, so eight times five equals forty.

cards.front: Do you have to put numbers in order to find the median?
cards.back: Yes. Put them in order first, then pick the middle one.
cards.say: Do you have to put numbers in order to find the median? Yes. Put them in order first, then pick the middle one.

cards.back: Cannot happen. Example: rolling a 7 on a normal dice. Probability 0.
cards.say: Impossible. Cannot happen. Example: rolling a seven on a normal dice. Probability zero.

cards.back: Not very likely to happen, but it could. Example: rolling a 6 on a dice is unlikely.
cards.say: Unlikely. Not very likely to happen, but it could. Example: rolling a six on a dice is unlikely.

cards.back: Just as likely to happen as not. Example: a coin landing on heads. Probability 1/2.
cards.say: Even chance. Just as likely to happen as not. Example: a coin landing on heads. Probability one half.

cards.back: More likely to happen than not. Example: picking a red ball from a bag of 9 red and 1 blue.
cards.say: Likely. More likely to happen than not. Example: picking a red ball from a bag of nine red and one blue.

cards.back: Will definitely happen. Example: rolling a number less than 7 on a normal dice. Probability 1.
cards.say: Certain. Will definitely happen. Example: rolling a number less than seven on a normal dice. Probability one.

cards.front: What numbers does the probability scale run from and to?
cards.back: From 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain).
cards.say: What numbers does the probability scale run from and to? From zero, impossible, to one, certain.

cards.front: Probability of heads when you flip a fair coin
cards.back: 1/2. There are 2 equally likely outcomes and 1 of them is heads.
cards.say: Probability of heads when you flip a fair coin. One half. There are two equally likely outcomes and one of them is heads.

cards.front: Probability of rolling a 6 on a fair dice
cards.back: 1/6. There are 6 equally likely outcomes and 1 of them is a 6.
cards.say: Probability of rolling a six on a fair dice. One sixth. There are six equally likely outcomes and one of them is a six.

cards.front: Probability of an even number on a fair dice
cards.back: 3/6, which is 1/2. The even numbers are 2, 4 and 6.
cards.say: Probability of an even number on a fair dice. Three sixths, which is one half. The even numbers are two, four and six.

cards.front: A bag has 3 red and 1 blue counter. Probability of blue?
cards.back: 1/4. One counter out of 4 is blue.
cards.say: A bag has three red and one blue counter. Probability of blue? One quarter. One counter out of four is blue.

cards.front: List all outcomes of flipping two coins
cards.back: HH, HT, TH, TT. That is 4 outcomes.
cards.say: List all outcomes of flipping two coins. Heads heads, heads tails, tails heads, tails tails. That is four outcomes.
